light penetration through treefall gaps in the temperate forests is more variable than in tropical forests, that the light regimes are more complex, that there is a larger range of light levels, that light penetration into treefall gaps varies more seasonally, and that there is more variation within a site than among sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no simple relationship between gap size and the amount of photosynthetically active light that reaches the forest floor.
the forest floor is a highly dynamic environment, with light levels changing rapidly and unpredictably over both diel and seasonal time scales.

the light environment in a forest is not simply a matter of whether or not the canopy is closed, but also a function of the canopy structure, and that this structure can be altered by human activities.
